questions.note: Hallux longest and toe 2 a little shorter; from above both are individually shaped, with bulbous tips and a PIP knuckle on toe 2. But the knuckle wrinkles are one identical parallel stamp, the DIP crease a cut, the pads boxy blocks with no pulp bulge, the hallux tip a chisel in profile, and a step seam crosses toe 2.

Plates, folds, a ~1 mm free edge and a straight trim are all there, but the hallux nail reads as a press-on acrylic: flat inset tile, white bevel at the root, opaque French-tip edge, no lunula, no pink bed. Toe 2's plate is brushed-metal streaks. Both hallux corners tear into sawtooth intersections and toe 2's corner drops into a slot.

Only the distal extensor tendons are in view: the EHL and the extensor ridges toward toe 2 read as soft relief catching the light, not drawn lines, but smooth and generic. No dorsal or digital veins show at the toe bases; the saphenous vein is in no view, so this rests on little.

Declared first pass, scored as seen. SSS is right: shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows. But the micro-relief is wrong in kind: an even crackle net of polygon cells everywhere, even through toe 2's nail, and plantar ridges as one straight corduroy field with no whorls; a wet sheen on the dorsum and no pores. It reads as silicone, not skin.

defects.what: Hallux nail, lateral distal corner: where the plate meets the lateral fold and hyponychium the surface breaks into a serrated sawtooth of tiny triangles running up the fold, a jagged white fringe visible even at native size (pair_hr.hallux_eval.png [1532,1180,1656,1346]).
defects.fix: On a real toe the lateral fold rolls smoothly over the plate's edge into a clean groove; skin and plate never cross, and the fold's rim stays one smooth curve to the free edge.

defects.what: Hallux nail, medial distal corner: dark, jagged teeth where the free edge, the medial fold and the hyponychium intersect; the clay shows the same torn geometry (pair_hr.hallux_form.png [952,1387,1097,1449]) and the medial view shows it at the tip.
defects.fix: The free edge overhangs the hyponychium with a clean dark gap, and the medial fold ends in a smooth, rounded corner beside it.

defects.what: 1–2 web, the hallux's lateral wall deep in the cleft: a column of torn, speckled triangles with terraced ripples below it; in the lit view it is a black jagged slit (pair_hr.toe2_eval.png [197,93,254,352]): surfaces crossing or collapsed in the cleft.
defects.fix: The web is one continuous skin saddle: the hallux's lateral wall curves smoothly down into the web floor and up toe 2's side, with soft creases and nothing folded or overlapping.

defects.what: Hallux plate, proximal and medial edges: a thick, bright-white bevel shows the plate's edge thickness at the root, so it reads as a stuck-on acrylic tile; no eponychium or cuticle laps over it and the plate does not vanish under the proximal fold.
defects.fix: A real plate slides out from under the proximal fold, so its root and edge thickness are never seen; a thin, slightly translucent cuticle band lies on the plate's base.

defects.what: Hallux free edge: an even, opaque, milk-white band with a rolled, wavy bead (clay zoom), like a French-manicure tip; no cut keratin face, no translucency at the margin, no yellowing and no grime line beneath.
defects.fix: A trimmed toenail edge is cut, slightly irregular off-white to yellowish keratin, translucent at the margin and square-faced in section, with a faint dark line under it.

defects.what: Hallux plate in clay: a flat tile with a template rounded-rectangle outline set in an even groove like an inset panel; almost no transverse curvature (the matcap is uniform across it), so in the medial view it reflects as one blown-out white slab.
defects.fix: A hallux plate curves across (about an 11 mm radius) and slightly lengthwise, its sides dip into the lateral grooves, and its outline is a little asymmetric, so the reflection grades across it.

defects.what: Hallux plate colour: one uniform milky grey-pink from root to free edge; no lunula, no pink bed reading through a clear plate, no paler band before the free edge, so it reads as frosted plastic laid on the toe.
defects.fix: A pale crescent lunula at the root, a pink bed showing through a mostly clear plate, a narrow paler band where the plate leaves the bed, and faint longitudinal tone variation.

defects.what: Toe 2 plate: covered edge to edge with dense, ruler-straight, high-contrast white streaks, a brushed-aluminium look, and the skin's polygon cell pattern shows through the plate as if the bed were dorsal skin.
defects.fix: Longitudinal ridges are faint and slightly wavy, seen mainly inside the highlight; the bed under the plate is smooth pink with fine lengthwise grooves, never the skin's cell network.

defects.what: Toe 2 nail, medial distal corner: the plate's corner drops into a dark, sharp-walled rectangular slot cut into the skin, visible at native size (pair_hr.toe2_eval.png [864,1465,911,1594]).
defects.fix: The lateral nail groove is a shallow, soft sulcus that opens out at the free edge, the fold's skin rounding over the plate's corner.

defects.what: From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded rectangles: straight parallel sides, square tips and flat faces, with no pulp bulge and no narrowing toward the flexion crease; tofu blocks, not pulps.
defects.fix: Real pulps are oval to teardrop cushions, fullest at the pulp centre, narrowing to a neck at the flexion crease, with round tips.

defects.what: Hallux in profile: the dorsal line slopes straight down to the nail's tip and the pulp is undercut beneath it, so the end reads as a chisel or beak instead of a blunt, rounded pulp.
defects.fix: The pulp carries forward and down under the free edge as a rounded bulb; in profile the tip is blunt, its front a convex curve below and ahead of the nail.

defects.what: 1–2 web margin: a long, straight, hard edge, a flat shelf jutting between the toes like a cut plane, with no saddle curve, no fold and no creases where the skin turns under to the plantar side.
defects.fix: The web's margin is a soft U-shaped saddle set back in the cleft, rounding under into the plantar web with a few fine creases.

defects.what: Hallux IP wrinkles (and toe 2's PIP set, [1196,637,1423,771]) are one stamp: 3–4 identical, evenly spaced, perfectly parallel grooves of equal depth, crisp in the clay too, like bellows rather than skin.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin bunches into irregular, branching, broken creases of mixed length and depth around an oval knuckle pad, with finer criss-cross lines between them.

defects.what: Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease: one long, even groove with a bright lip running across the whole toe, reading as a knife cut.
defects.fix: A DIP shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases that fade at the toe's sides, shallower than the PIP set.

defects.what: Toe 2, plantar middle phalanx: a crisp ring-like step crosses the toe between the flexion creases, with smooth skin above it and ridged skin below (pair_hr.plantar_eval.png [616,983,932,1040]); the distal part reads as a thimble glued on.
defects.fix: Skin runs continuously along the toe: no step and no change of texture between the creases; only the true flexion creases mark the plantar side.

defects.what: Under the hallux's base the plantar outline is pinched into a sharp V-notch with a hard lip, a crimp in the silhouette as if the toe were a tube joined to the foot; the clay shows the same.
defects.fix: The digito-plantar crease is a soft fold: the toe's pad bulges down and meets the ball in a rounded groove.

defects.what: Dorsum of the hallux's base (1st MTP): a single long, sharp-lipped groove crosses it like a healed incision, not a flexion crease.
defects.fix: Dorsal MTP creases are several soft, shallow, wavy lines, deepest when the toe extends, never one sharp groove.

defects.what: A small round bead sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold at the plate's medial corner, a lump that follows no anatomy (also pair_hr.top34_form.png [1097,1201,1144,1237] and pair_hr.front_form.png).
defects.fix: The eponychium is an even, continuous rim along the plate's root, with no bulges.

defects.what: Pinch marks dimple both pulps' tips in the clay like mesh poles: a short crease and a faint transverse line on the hallux pulp, an X-shaped pinch on toe 2's ([673,1408,725,1480]).
defects.fix: Each pulp is an even cushion; the only marks on it are its friction ridges.

defects.what: Toe 2's medial side: a thin bright ridge runs from the DIP crease to the nail fold like a mould parting line.
defects.fix: The lateral nail fold fades softly into the side of the toe with no crisp lengthwise edge.

ranked: [D6] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a flat tile in a template rounded-rectangle outline sunk in an even groove like an inset panel; with almost no transverse curve it reflects as one blown-out white slab from the side.

[D4] Its root shows a thick white bevel, the plate's own edge thickness, with no cuticle or eponychium lapping over it: a stuck-on acrylic nail. A real plate slides out from under the proximal fold and its root is never seen.

[D1] Both distal corners of the hallux nail tear into sawtooth fringes where plate, folds and hyponychium intersect, white teeth up the lateral fold and dark teeth at the medial corner [D2]; visible at native size in every view of the nail and unmistakably CG.
[D10] From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded rectangles with straight sides, square tips and flat faces, no pulp bulge and no neck at the crease; they read as silicone blocks, not pulps.

The declared first-pass skin distorts the pads: the plantar ridges are one field of straight, parallel diagonal stripes at a single angle across both pulps and the sole, like corduroy, with no whorls or loops; in the medial view they band the toe like contour lines.

[D5] The hallux free edge is an even, opaque, milk-white band with a rolled, wavy bead: a French-manicure tip. A trimmed toenail edge is cut, slightly irregular, translucent off-white keratin with a faint grime line under it.

[D13] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: 3–4 identical, evenly spaced, perfectly parallel grooves of equal depth, like bellows; real knuckle skin bunches into irregular, branching, broken creases of mixed depth.

[D11] In profile the hallux tapers to a chisel: the dorsal line runs straight to the nail's tip and the pulp is undercut beneath it, where a real big toe ends in a blunt, round pulp below and ahead of the free edge.
[D3] Deep in the 1–2 web the hallux's lateral wall is torn: a column of broken, speckled triangles over terraced ripples in the clay, a black jagged slit in the lit toe 2 view.

[D8] Toe 2's plate is streaked edge to edge with dense, ruler-straight, high-contrast white lines, brushed aluminium rather than keratin, and the skin's cell net shows through it as if the bed were dorsal skin.

The declared first-pass skin also hides the toes' surface: an even crackle-glaze net of equal polygon cells covers everything, crisp on toe 2 and the web and faint on the hallux, under a wet sheen and with no pores; real toe skin has fine oriented furrows and smoother tips.
[D7] The hallux plate is one milky grey-pink from root to edge: no lunula, no pink bed under a clear plate, no paler band before the free edge, so it reads as frosted plastic laid on the toe.

[D12] The 1–2 web's margin is a long, straight, hard edge, a flat shelf jutting between the toes like a cut plane; a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle set back in the cleft, curling under to the plantar side.
[D15] A crisp ring-like step crosses toe 2's plantar middle phalanx between its creases, smooth above and ridged below, so the tip reads as a thimble glued on where two meshes or methods meet.

[D16] Under the hallux's base the plantar outline is pinched into a sharp V-notch with a hard lip, as if the toe were a tube joined to the foot; the digito-plantar crease is a soft fold under a bulging pad.
[D14] Toe 2's dorsal DIP crease is a single long, even groove with a bright lip, a knife cut rather than the two or three short, soft creases a real DIP shows.
[D9] Toe 2's nail drops its medial distal corner into a dark, sharp-walled slot in the skin, where the nail groove should be a soft sulcus opening out at the free edge.
[D17] A single long, sharp-lipped groove crosses the dorsum of the hallux's base like a healed incision; dorsal MTP creases are several soft, shallow, wavy lines.

The toes read younger and cleaner than a boot-wearing 40-year-old's: pristine template nails with no thickening, trim marks or wear, perfectly even folds, and no hair tuft on the hallux or toe 2 (hair is outside this round): a mannequin or prosthetic read.
[D18] A small round bead sits on the hallux's proximal fold at the plate's medial corner in all three clay views, a lump that follows no anatomy.
[D19] Pinch marks dimple both pulps' tips in the clay, like mesh poles: a short crease on the hallux pulp and an X-shaped pinch on toe 2's.
[D20] A thin bright ridge runs along toe 2's medial side from the DIP crease to the nail fold, like a mould parting line.
